priority.when: Always use first to find existing plans
priority.why: Discover what plans already exist in plans/ directory
Understand current plan structure and dependencies

priority.when: Need to find specific implementation details
priority.why: Understand how components work before planning changes

tool.name: apply_diff

best_practices.practice: Always read the plan file first to ensure exact content match
Make multiple changes in one diff when possible

tool.example: <apply_diff> <path>plans/new-feature-plan.md</path> <diff> <<<<<<< SEARCH :start_line:10 ------- ## Planned Changes - [ ] Task 1 - [ ] Task 2 ======= ## Planned Changes - [ ] Task 1 - Detailed description - [ ] Task 2 - Detailed description - [ ] Task 3 - Additional task >>>>>>> REPLACE </diff> </apply_diff>

tool.name: ask_followup_question

best_practices.practice: Order suggestions by likelihood or importance

tool.example: <ask_followup_question> <question>Which plan file would you like me to create or modify?</question> <follow_up> <item> <text>Create a new plan for Nix packaging improvements</text> <mode>null</mode> </item> <item> <text>Update the existing systemd service definitions plan</text> <mode>null</mode> </item> <item> <text>Review the navigation rules plan for consistency</text> <mode>null</mode> </item> </follow_up> </ask_followup_question>

best_practices.practice: Use to verify file existence or check git status
Use for project-wide operations like finding files

action.name: create_plan
action.description: Creating a new plan file following the template

steps.step: Use the standard template from navigation rules
Fill in purpose and scope sections
Read the existing plan to understand current state
Update planned changes checkboxes as appropriate

action.name: review_plan
action.description: Reviewing a plan for compliance with navigation rules

steps.step: Check that all required sections are present
Validate entry points are specific and accurate
